overloadMerges.note: The two doc syntax lines are alternate optional trailing arguments of one operation, not two distinct overloads: offset (write-at-position, returning the updated offset) and * (append-at-end) are mutually exclusive ways to pick where the Integer is written. Also fixed offset's direction to 'inout' per the parameter table's '<->' arrow (it is read on input and overwritten with the new offset on output).

params.name: integer
params.description: 2-byte Integer value to write into the BLOB.

params.name: blob
params.description: BLOB to receive the Integer value; the legacy Blob type only, not a 4D.Blob object, since this command alters the blob in place.

params.name: byteOrder
params.description: Byte ordering to use when writing the value.

params.name: offset
params.description: In: byte offset (from the start of the BLOB) at which to write the value. Out: updated to the offset just past the bytes written, so it can be reused for a subsequent BLOB-writing call.
If passed, the value is appended after the BLOB's current end instead of written at a fixed position, growing the BLOB accordingly.

overloadMerges.semanticRole: Writes a 2-byte Integer value into a BLOB, either overwriting its start (if neither offset nor * is passed), at a given byte offset (advancing that offset for reuse), or appended to its end.

jointConstraints.rule: offset and * are mutually exclusive: pass at most one of them. Passing neither writes the value at the beginning of the BLOB, overriding its previous contents.

constraints: Newly allocated bytes other than the ones being written (e.g. a gap before an offset beyond the current BLOB size) are initialized to zero.
It is up to the caller to manage byte-order swapping when exchanging BLOBs written this way between Macintosh and PC platforms.
